### E6 the levers: what it settles, and where it deviated (2026-10-28, not yet committed)

Built from `docs/qa/2026-10-24/e6-levers-design.md` on HEAD `8da8c2a` (save v56), in the order of authority the queue set: the DIRECTOR ANSWER (**Q-A (a):** Earth cannot embargo a live pact partner; R8, the lift, is not built; **Q-B (a):** a sabotage stops the target's production for the six whole sols after the act, `SabotageCutPct` 100; **Q-C (a):** only a betrayed partner charges a tariff: 2,500 bp, every resource, both ways, 30 sols) > `docs/qa/2026-10-26/preflight/ORCHESTRATOR-RULINGS.md` (ruling 1: no gate asserts its frame is the last; ruling 6: the wording prefix Z; ruling 7: `git grep -P`; ruling 8: v57) > `CROSS-CHECK.md` section 6 (items 1, 2, 6, 7, 9, 15, 16, 17) > `E6-brief.md` > the design's REFRESH, REVISION, re-review, review and body. The brief's anchors were at `d842dd0`; E5 moved H, M, W, K and the click test, and every reference was re-anchored by symbol (H: E4's politics hooks 1617-1621 -> 1683-1687, the four sets 3947 / 3976 / 3988-3989 -> 4164 / 4193 / 4205-4206; M: `RollMarket` 509 -> 516, `MarketProduceAndReprice` 560 -> 586, `ClearConvoy` 639 -> 665, `GetOrderReservationMcr` 826 -> 901, `PlanConvoy` 851 -> 926, `CanPlaceOrder` 1027 -> 1125, `BookConvoy` 1041 -> 1140, the goodwill check 1236 -> 1351; W: the covert dispatch 9585 / 9595 / 9605 -> 9631 / 9641 / 9651, `ResolveCovert` 9795 -> 9841, `ResolveLaunder` 9865 -> 9911, `ResolveSabotage` 9904 -> 9950, `StepEarth` -> 10010, `StepPreemptive` 10081 -> 10131, `ResolvePacify` 10151 -> 10201, `ResolveDilemma` 10347 -> 10399, the v21 / v22 writes 13708-13726 -> 13776-13782, the tail after `'RHE5'` 13928-13933 -> 13991, the mid-file reads 14361-14385 -> 14433-14441; K: the rival card 2355 -> 2399, `HandleOrderNudge` 2646 -> 3025; V 4249-4251 -> 4977-4979; the click test's market step 1754 -> 1890). E5 as built, against the brief's A1-A10: the `'RHE5'` frame is written at W:13991 and read straight after `ReadMarketBlock`, then `ReconcileReservations()` (A1); the journal is `FRHPoliticalEntry` with `ERHPoliticalAct { Defy, Comply, Pacify, Issue, Withdraw }`, to which E6 appends `PactSign` and `PactBreak` (A2); `ResolveDilemma` and `ResolvePacify` take the command, the three covert resolvers did not, and E6 gives them `const FRHCommand&` (A3); `CanExchange`'s check 3 read the three sets directly (RHSimCurrency.cpp:506), and so did `CanIssueCurrency` (:381), a reader the brief's table does not name (T8): both now read `IsRouteClosed` / `HasDefected` / `IsEmbargoed` (A4); the mark as the brief describes (A5); `PlanConvoy` already takes E5's clearing sol, reused as EffSol (A6); `BlocStance`, `Debug_SyncPoliticalView()`, `GetCurrencyBlockBytes()` and CU8's harness exist (A7); `bMarketBlockLost` exists and is not needed (A8); the baseline is `Saved/baselines/battery_post_e5` (59 runs) (A9); MX1's compare is bounded to the market frame (A10). After E6, `git grep -n -P '\b(ClosedRoutes|SabotageSols|EmbargoGrace|DefectedRivals)\b' Source` is empty (the load's temporaries are named `Mirror*`; `GetEmbargoGrace` and the config's `EmbargoGraceSols` keep their names).

**What E6 builds.** (Every number below is a placeholder awaiting the director.)
- **One list of trade rules** (`TArray<FRHTradeRule> TradeRules`, ascending by Id; `NextRuleId` saved, from 1, never reused) replaces HEAD's `ClosedRoutes`, `SabotageSols`, `EmbargoGrace` and `DefectedRivals`. Kinds `Closed` 1, `Disrupted` 2, `Severed` 3, `Embargo` 4 (the refusal precedence), `Pact` 5, `Tariff` 6; origins `Comply` 1, `Sabotage` 2, `Defection` 3, `EarthPressure` 4, `Signed` 5, `Betrayal` 6, `Harness` 7. Windows are half-open `[From, Until)`: none `(-1, -1)`, closed, or open-ended (`Until -1`); each kind has its legal shapes (D8) and its exclusivity (D9). A repeated sabotage **appends** a rule. One walk, `EvaluateTradeRules(Rival, EffSol, Lines)`, gives the block (the lowest kind among the live blocking rules, then the lowest Id, with HEAD's text for that kind), each line's markup (the sum of the covering tariffs, clamped to `TariffMaxBp`) and whether a pact window covers EffSol; the market never reads a live timer, a live flag or an Id. `PlanConvoy` (so `Convoy`, `MarketOrder`, `CanPlaceOrder`, `CanPlaceStandingOrder`) and `CanSignPact` take the walk's block; E5's desk reads only `Closed`, `Severed` and `Embargo` (sabotage never refuses the desk, R7). The countdowns are HEAD's arithmetic statement for statement (the same `DtSols`, the same function and point, tested `<= 0.0`): `StepEarth` counts each live `Disrupted` rule down in Id order and raises HEAD's `RECOVERED` alert when a rival's last one ends; `StepPreemptive` counts each `Embargo` down and hardens it into a `Severed` rule in place (its Id kept, origin `Defection`). Retirement runs at the very end of `RollMarket` (D10 with re-review O2). The goodwill check reads the list (`Severed`, `Embargo`, `Closed`).
- **Pacts.** A new uplink verb `Treaty` (`Target` the neighbour, `Text` `Sign` or `Break`, any case). `CanSignPact` refuses in D16's order with its texts (Z5). Signing, at execution: Influence -15, Earth tension +5 (journaled +5,000, so the mark's rate reads it at the sol's close), HumanNature +3, a live `Pact` rule `[c + 2, open)`, one alert and the log line. A pact whose window covers an order's EffSol raises that order's cargo cap from `ConvoyCargoKg` (1,000) to `PactCargoKg` (2,000) each way (a barter neighbour's lots are fixed). A Break, at execution: the pact's live part ends and its window closes at `max(c + 2, From)`; relation -25, HumanNature -10, tension -5 (journaled -5,000); the betrayal tariff (Q-C a): 2,500 bp on every resource both ways, `[c + 2, c + 32)`, origin `Betrayal` (never above `TariffMaxBp`: the config's one cross-row rule, `ClampBetrayalTariffToMax` in `InitLevers`, and a clamp where the rule is made, so no load repair ever rewrites it). A Comply that closes a partner's route ends the pact with no tariff (`=== PACT ENDED ... ===`); a caught covert op or sabotage against a partner ends it from the partner's side with the betrayal tariff and no further relation or HumanNature change (`=== PACT BROKEN by %s: they caught you ===`); a clean op leaves it standing. **Q-A (a):** `StepPreemptive`'s target filter skips a rival with a live pact, so Earth embargoes the next eligible neighbour or nobody; nothing lifts an embargo (R8 not built).
- **Tariffs, integer only.** `tariff = ceil(value x m / 10000)`, a buy costs `value + tariff`, a sell receives `value - tariff` (`MarketTariffMcr`, `MarketLineSettleMcr`); with `m = 0` every figure is E4's and E5's to the milli-unit. The reservation is `HiM = Hi + ceil(Hi x m)`, `LoM = max(0, Lo - ceil(Lo x m))`, then E5's `HiR` / `LoR` for a credit order after the issue. `ValueMcr` (the goodwill floor), E4's tally and E5's bloc tally stay at the clearing price before the markup. `TariffPaidMcr` counts the orders cleared before the market counts in marks, `TariffPaidMmk` those cleared while it does (in the market's unit). No markup is negative and the desk carries none. The clearing charges the markup recomputed at the stored EffSol (`max(ClearSol, MarketCheckedSol)` at booking, kept per uncleared priced convoy in E6's own payload, never in `'RHE4'`); the booking markups are stored only so LV8 can assert the two are equal (T3).
- **Covert acts that move the market.** A sabotage's new `Disrupted` rule gets the market window `[c + 1, c + 1 + SabotageMarketSols)` (6): at every roll closing a sol inside a rival's windows its production is cut by `SabotageCutPct` (100, Q-B a) in both of E4's uses (the store, and step 3's Prod term), computed locally (T2: `ProdSumG` and `ProduceG` are never written), consumption going on; the live refusal is HEAD's (6 sols on the timer), caught or not. A clean `Covert` against a rival with an economy records one pending `Theft` per looted resource, and a `Launder` one pending `Offering` per slot it spent, keyed by the act's own sol, `CommandId` and slot order; a caught op and a barter rival record nothing. The roll applies every effect due, in `(ClearSol, CommandId, Sub)` order, after the convoy and desk clearing and the ring advance, before production and outside the live gate (a theft takes `min(grams, store)`); neither kind enters a tally. The covert roll is untouched (no new `RollCovertDetected`, `CovertAttempts` and the roll's inputs as HEAD's).
- **The switch.** `bLeversEnabled` (runtime only, default on, `Debug_SetLeversEnabled`): off, `Treaty` is refused, no effect is recorded, a `Disrupted` rule gets no window and every markup reads 0; the roll reads it too (3.3: `RollMarket`'s cut windows and `GetRivalCutPct`), so a window made while the levers were on cuts nothing while they are off (LV6). LV1 (d) reads each of the four gates directly (a later gate can hide an earlier one: a window made with the levers off would still cut nothing, since the roll reads the switch too). The migration is not switchable. E4's five politics hooks are rebuilt on the list with origin `Harness` (D30), so MX11 does not move.
- **Save v57.** E6's payload sits in its own frame `'RHL6'`, written straight after E5's `'RHE5'` and read after E5's reader (and after `ReconcileReservations`): FormatRev 1, `NextRuleId`, the rules by Id (names as strings; `*` for every resource), the pending effects, the two lifetime tariff totals, and the terms of every uncleared priced convoy (EffSol and one booking markup per line). A default colony's block is 33 bytes, so every save grows by 53 (12 + 33 + 8). The v19, v21 and v22 slots stay, byte for byte in HEAD's layout, as a mirror projected from the rules (D31); a lost or malformed block rebuilds the rules from the mirror (D33: `Closed` by name string, then `Severed`, `Embargo`, and `Disrupted` with no window), with one Warning naming what is lost. Every other repair is a Warning and the colony always loads (Z8); no load path logs an Error.
- **Presentation (minimal; E8 is the full panel).** On each neighbour's card: the pact row (`Sign a pact (15 Influence)` with `SIGN`, greyed by `CanSignPact` with the reason on a dim line under the row, `Cannot sign a pact now: %s.`, and in its tooltip, as E5's issue button shows its own; or, with a live pact, `Pact since sol %d` - the sol it was signed in, `GetLivePactSignedSol`, always one already reached - with ` (bigger convoys from sol %d)` while the pact's window is still ahead of the market's open sol, and `BREAK`); the tooltips name every cost and when each term starts (SIGN: the Influence, the tension and the conduct shift +3, Earth's protection once it lands, the colony's bigger convoys to them from two sols after; BREAK: the standing -25, the conduct shift -10, the tension -5, and the tariff from two sols after it lands); the amber tariff line (`Tariff %s until sol %d`) and the disruption line (`Production stopped until sol %d`), each naming its first sol too while its window has not opened (`Tariff 25% from sol 2 until sol 31`), and the disruption line's word following the config's cut (`stopped` at `SabotageCutPct` 100, `cut N%` otherwise, no line at 0) (Z1-Z3); a percentage is printed exactly (`FormatPercentBp`: 2500 `25%`, 2550 `25.5%`), never `Bp / 100` truncated, here and in `PACT BROKEN`'s alert and log line; the order's name `Pact`, and on the uplink list `Pact <neighbour> (sign)` / `(break)` (Z4); the order draft's per-line clamp is the sim's own cap for an order sent now (`GetOrderCargoCapKg`: `PactCargoKg` when a pact's window covers the sol that order would clear in, else `ConvoyCargoKg`; the brief's P7). Console `RH.Treaty <Rival> sign|break` and `RH.Levers` (Z9; `, ended` follows a tariff only once its window is behind the open sol).

**UNCERTAIN items of the brief, each with its stated default taken.**
- **T1, "every resource" in the save:** the sentinel `*` (never `""`, which `RHSaveFrame::ReadName` refuses), pinned in LV9.
- **T6, displayed end sols:** a half-open window names its last sol, `Until - 1`, everywhere a player or a log reads it (the tariff line, the disruption line, `PACT BROKEN`'s "from sol %d to sol %d", `CanSignPact`'s "(until sol %d)").
- **Section 3.4, the rows the spec gives no clamp:** every one of the 13 rows is clamped (`LeversConfigClamp`, one table for the sim and LV0): the relation, tension and HumanNature rows 0..100, `PactInfluenceCost` 0..1000, `PactCargoKg` 1..10,000 (E5's rate step multiplies the 8-sol bloc tally by 10^4: its int64 bound, `8 x 3 x cap x 4 x 900,000 x 10^4`, holds up to about 10,700 kg; the first build's 1..1,000,000 did not), `PactBetrayalTariffBp` and `TariffMaxBp` 0..9999 (so a sale can never turn into a charge), with the one cross-row rule `PactBetrayalTariffBp <= TariffMaxBp`, `PactBetrayalTariffSols` 1..1000, `SabotageMarketSols` 1..30, `SabotageCutPct` 0..100; LV0 probes 26 values against them, pins the cross-row rule, and runs `InitLevers` itself on all 13 rows out of range (each held clamped, the betrayal tariff at the cap).
- **Section 8, a pact step in the click test:** added, as recommended (the deviation below).
- **Section 7, a `-currency` line that prints an unmasked whole-file size:** none moved (the battery below).
- **A6:** E5's `PlanConvoy` already takes the clearing sol (its `EffSol` parameter), so E6 reuses it and adds none.

**Deviations** (each kept as small as the gate allowed):
- **The effect's `CommandId` is saved as an int32**, not widened to int64 as the brief's section 4 lays it out: `CROSS-CHECK.md` item 9 (which outranks the brief) allows matching E5's journal, and `FRHCommand` holds an int32. The effect is 4 bytes shorter.
- **A stored EffSol that is not `max(ClearSol, MarketCheckedSol)` is re-derived from the convoy silently**, not with repair 11's Warning, whichever side it falls on (the first two builds re-derived only one below the clearing sol; one past it - only a resealed file holds one - would have made the clearing read markups at a sol its reservation was not booked for). An uncleared convoy's EffSol is exactly that value (booked at `max(ClearSol, the open sol then)`, and no roll has closed its clearing sol since, or it would have cleared), so a consistent save never meets the repair. **Why silent, exactly:** E4's block is authoritative for the convoy and accepts a moved clearing sol without a word, and E5's CU9 moves one on purpose and asserts that the load logs no Warning at all (`RHSimCurrencySuite.cpp:1565`, `bQuiet`): a Warning here does not just add a line to `currency.log` (cross-check item 16), it **fails CU9** (the first build's Warning did: `quick1/currency.log`, "CURRENCY FAIL: CU9 ... [first failing condition: #1]"). LV9 asserts the silence on both sides (`lv9c2` EffSol - 3, `lv9c6` EffSol + 3; mutation 30). A terms entry whose convoy E4's reader dropped, or whose market block was lost, is dropped silently too (ruling 1 (2), cross-check item 2); the Warning stays for a terms entry whose convoy loaded and disagrees in its line count, or has cleared. **For the orchestrator:** cross-check item 2 ("keep the Warning only for a terms entry whose convoy loaded but disagrees (LineCount, EffSol)") cannot hold its EffSol half once E5's CU9 exists; ruling 1 (2) adopted item 2 so that `market.log` and `currency.log` gain no Warnings, and item 16 requires `currency.log` line-identical. This build keeps the LineCount Warning and makes the EffSol repair silent. Accept that in writing at commit, or amend item 2 to drop "EffSol", so D6e, D7 or E8 does not restore the Warning and turn CU9 red.
- **A `Tariff` rule carries `bLive` false and a non-tariff rule `Dir` 3**: neither field means anything for that kind, so each is made with one fixed value (the loader takes them as read: they change nothing).
- **Load repairs beyond section 4's list**, each a Warning and each exercised in LV9: a markup on any kind but a tariff is set to 0 (only a tariff carries one; `lv9r9`, a closed route's 500 bp); a live timer on a kind that has none (`Closed`, `Severed`, `Pact`, `Tariff`) is set to 0 (`lv9t7`, a pact's 3 sols); a disruption whose window the upper clamp empties keeps no window and its live part (`lv9w11`), and a tariff it empties is dropped (`lv9w10`).
- **Four small load and clearing hardenings the review asked for** (none moves a gate line): a load raises `NextCommandId` past every pending effect's `CommandId` (E5's trap 7 extended: a fresh process's next act never takes a pending one's Id; LV9); a `NextRuleId` below `max(1, the last rule's Id + 1)` or above 2^30 makes the block malformed, the rules then rebuilt from the mirror (repair 1, now also for a frame with no rule; LV9); an embargo beside a defection is dropped by a `RemoveAll` whose predicate reads a set gathered first, never the array it compacts; and `ClearConvoy`'s no-terms case (no path makes one) reads `max(ClearSol, the closing sol)`, the loader's default, with its booking markups left empty, so a test comparing the booking and clearing markups can never compare a verdict with itself.
- **The load Warnings name a kind with its article** (`an embargo`, `a pact`); the first build printed `a embargo`.
- **SIGN's reason is also printed under the pact row** (`Cannot sign a pact now: %s.`, dim, while `CanSignPact` refuses), not only in its tooltip as the brief has it: E4's SEND ORDER and E5's DEFY, AND ISSUE and desk SEND all show a greyed button's reason on a visible line, and the first build's card read as if Influence were the gate when the relation was (the review's finding). It costs the card two lines while a pact cannot be signed.
- **`Pact since sol N` prints the sol the pact was signed in** (`GetLivePactSignedSol` = the window's first sol - 2). The spec gives the text but never defines N; the first build printed the window's first sol, a sol still ahead for two sols after a signing. While that window is still ahead of the market's open sol the row adds ` (bigger convoys from sol %d)`.
- **The card names a term's first sol while it is still ahead** (`Tariff 25% from sol 2 until sol 31`, `Production stopped from sol 1 until sol 6`, the pact's `(bigger convoys from sol 2)`), beyond the spec's texts (`25% until sol 91`, `production stopped until sol 66`), so a term the act has scheduled never reads as one in force (design risk 1: both clocks legible). Once the window covers the market's open sol the line is the spec's.
- **The disruption line's word follows `SabotageCutPct`**: `Production stopped` at 100 (the authored value, Q-B a), `Production cut %d%%` at any other value, no line at 0 or with the harness's levers off. The spec's text assumes 100.
- **Percentages are printed exactly** (`FormatPercentBp`: 2500 `25%`, 2550 `25.5%`, 2505 `25.05%`), on the card, in BREAK's tooltip, and in `PACT BROKEN`'s alert and log line, where the brief's D19 has `they charge %d%%` (`Bp / 100`, truncated). The default config prints the same text either way.
- **The order draft's clamp is the sim's cap for an order sent now** (`GetOrderCargoCapKg`: the walk's pact flag at `GetBookingSolNow()`, the sol PlanConvoy itself reads), not `HasLivePact`, which the brief's section 3.9 parenthetical names. The live flag opens two sols before the window and closes two sols before it ends (`EndPact` keeps `[From, c + 2)`), so the deck held drafts to 2,000 kg two sols early and to 1,000 kg for the two sols an ended pact still carries 2,000; the walk's flag closes both edges.
- **The signing's alert is headed `PACT SIGNED`** (the first build's `A PACT`), mirroring `PACT BROKEN` and keeping the corrected sentence on one banner line at 1440x860 (Z6; placeholder wording).
- **The mirror rebuild's origins:** a rule rebuilt from the mid-file record takes the origin its kind is made with in play (`Closed` from `Comply`, `Severed` from `Defection`, `Embargo` from `EarthPressure`, `Disrupted` from `Sabotage`); an embargo beside a rebuilt defection is skipped (D9).
- **A party name differing only in case** is read as its row with a Warning (repair 3). UE's `FString ==` ignores case, so the loader compares with `ESearchCase::CaseSensitive`; the first build did not, and LV9's case-only fixture caught it.
- **Transient records are trimmed:** the effects as applied and the production cuts (for tests and the deck) keep the newest 64, trimmed whenever they pass 128 (amortised, so a roll never shifts the array) and keeping their capacity (`EAllowShrinking::No`, as the pending effects' queue does when it applies one), and `RollMarket` walks the rules once per pass for both the cut windows and whether anything can retire (it retires only then). This round also moved the retirement test, `TradeRuleRetiresAt`, into the header as an inline function, body unchanged: under the adaptive build the modified `RHSimMarket.cpp` and `RHSimLevers.cpp` are separate translation units, so `RollMarket`'s walk made one out-of-line call per rule per roll (60 in `-scale`), and inlining it took the E6 line from 1.080 / 1.110 / 1.070 ms to 0.958 / 0.962 / 1.027 on otherwise identical sources, every digest identical. All are for `-scale` (below); none is saved.
- **More hooks and getters than the brief names**, all for the tests and the deck: `Debug_EnqueueAt` (an uplink order at a given execution time, appended, to build the era band's queue inversion), `Debug_SetRelation`, `Debug_RemoveRule`, `Debug_AddTradeRule`, `Debug_AddMarketEffect`, `GetLedgerSlotIndex`, `GetCovertAttempts`, `GetMarketEffectsApplied`, `GetProductionCuts`, `GetDisruptionUntilSol`, `GetDisruptionWindow` (the windows still ahead as one span: they never leave a gap), `GetLivePactFromSol`, `GetLivePactSignedSol`, `GetBetrayalTariff` (with its first sol, optional), `GetOrderCargoCapKg` (the draft's clamp), `GetSabotageCutPct`, `IsLeversBlockLost`, `GetLeversConfig`, `LeversConfigClamp`, `FormatPercentBp`, `Debug_SetTariffConfig` (LV0: the two tariff rows through their clamps and the cross-row rule) and `Debug_InitLeversWith` (LV0: `InitLevers` itself with rows given in place of the config's, through the same body, `InitLeversFrom`); the cost getters for the deck's tooltips (`GetPactHumanNatureShift` and `GetPactBreakHumanNatureShift` among them). Each `Debug_` hook is harness-only, as HEAD's.

**Findings.**
- **UE's `FString ==` ignores case.** The first build's case-only party check compared names with `!=` and never warned; LV9's case-only fixture caught it. The loader and the suite now compare with `ESearchCase::CaseSensitive`.
- **`-scale` was over budget on the first build:** 1.203 ms against the same run's E5 line 0.876 + 0.2 (then 1.157 and 1.168 against 0.933 and 0.942). Three changes, none of which moves a result: the transient records are trimmed in amortised steps (no shift of the whole array at every roll), a 100% cut skips the multiply, and `RollMarket` walks the rules once a pass for the cut windows and for whether anything can retire. Then 1.097 / 1.033 / 1.146 against 0.930 / 0.884 / 0.959, and 1.035 / 1.061 / 1.029 against 0.909 / 0.905 / 0.900 on the build the mutations started from.
- **The first build warned when a stored EffSol fell below its convoy's clearing sol.** E5's CU9 moves a convoy's clearing sol on purpose (E4 accepts it silently) and asserts that the load logs no Warning at all (`RHSimCurrencySuite.cpp:1565`, `bQuiet`), so the Warning did not just add an unlisted line to `currency.log`: it failed CU9 (`quick1/currency.log`: `LoadColony v57: the terms of convoy #1 clear in sol 2, before its clearing sol 3; raised to 3`, then `CURRENCY FAIL: CU9 ... [first failing condition: #1]`). The re-derivation is silent (the deviation above), now on both sides, and LV9 asserts it.
- **A restored mutation must be newer than its object** (E5's finding): the LV12 driver restores each source by copy with a fresh file time and checks its sha256, so UBT recompiles it; the final binary was built from the restored sources, `-DisableAdaptiveUnity` first.
- **The second review's blocking findings, and what they were** (fixed in the second round): (1) LV6's second sabotage ran after `RollNext` alone, which rolls the market but never steps `StepEarth`, so the first rule's timer was still 6 when the second landed and neither the max in `GetSabotageRemaining` nor the single `RECOVERED` at the last overlapping rule's end was exercised anywhere in `-levers`; with real era steps both are pinned now (mutations 19 and 20 turn them red). (2) The first gate's battery ran with `RH_BATTERY_LOGDIR` redirected, so `Saved/RHBattery` still held E5's 59 logs: the brief's freshness test and its diff read E5's logs (that diff compared the base with itself, TOTAL 0), and a `battery_post_e6` snapshot taken the handoff's way would have frozen E5's logs into D6e's base. This gate's battery ran in the default directory.
- **`-scale`'s E6 margin was thin, and the trims cost a reallocation.** On this gate's first final build (`dcd06cff...`), six `-scale` runs at a load average of 4-7 put the E6 line 0.18, 0.25, 0.19, -0.17 (E5's line spiked), 0.17 and 0.15 ms above the same run's E5 line: run 2 failed the E6 budget (1.239 ms against 0.991 + 0.2); runs 1, 3, 4 and 5 also missed HEAD's own wall-clock budgets (run 1 both cold commutes, 12.764 and 10.920 ms against 10; run 3 the cold deep net, 3.9985 against 3; run 4 a cold commute, 11.925; run 5 the cold deep net, 4.6208), the same budgets HEAD's binary misses under load (above); run 6 was clean. The production-cut record, trimmed back to 64 every eight rolls with every rival cut, also shrank its allocation each time and grew it back, two or three reallocations per trim; trimming without shrinking took the gap to 0.12, 0.16 and 0.11 ms at the same load, and the gate below was re-run from the build on that change (the twelve mutations of `RHSimMarket.cpp` and `RHSimLevers.cpp` included). The superseded runs' logs are kept in the session scratchpad (`gate2a_superseded/`).
- **`PactCargoKg`'s first clamp (1..1,000,000) broke E5's int64 bound** on the rate step's bloc-tally product above about 10,700 kg a convoy (signed overflow); it is 1..10,000 now. E4's `ConvoyCargoKg` has no upper clamp of its own (below).
- **The first gate's mutation 4 was never seen failing its named per-order sub-check** (LV8's check stops at its first failing condition, #2); LV8 now prints its per-order sub-checks on an info line whatever the outcome, and under mutation 4 the era twin's booking == clearing comparison is red there.
- **The third review's blocking finding: LV7's "a barter rival records nothing" could not fail.** Its covert op ran by day at the injected rival's relation 30, so P was 0.425 against its U of 0.422 at attempt 2 (the roll is deterministic: the same in every run), and the op was caught every time; a caught op never reaches `RecordMarketEffects`, so the assertion held only because a caught op records nothing (already condition #2), and no check sent a Launder to a barter rival either. The op now runs at relation 60 (P 0.35: clean, its `COVERT CLEAN` line asserted) and a Launder follows it; mutation 24, which drops both of the recorder's barter guards, turns LV7 red (`leaves 1 pending effects, its launder 2`).
- **Three of D29's four gates had no check that could see them** (the review's finding): no levers-off state ever held a tariff, so the markup gate in `EvaluateTradeRules` could be deleted unseen; the sabotage-window gate was hidden behind the roll's own switch read (an off-twin window still cuts nothing); and `CanBreakPact`'s disabled refusal was never reached. LV1 (d) now reads each gate directly, and mutations 27-29 turn it red.
- **Repair 11 re-derived only an EffSol below the convoy's clearing sol**, so a resealed file with an EffSol past `max(ClearSol, the open sol)` kept it, and the clearing could charge a markup its reservation never covered; any EffSol that is not that value is re-derived now (silently, as before; mutation 30). **`InitLevers`' clamps and its cross-row call were never run on out-of-range rows** (LV0 probed the clamp table directly); `Debug_InitLeversWith` runs `InitLevers`' own body (mutations 25 and 26). **LV9 left repair 8's second defection and second embargo, the cleared-convoy terms branch, the builder's own extra repairs and D33's rebuild order unchecked**; each is checked now (mutations 31 and 32 for the kind list and the order).
- **This round's first final build missed the `-scale` budget, and the cause was an out-of-line call per rule.** Its gate (part A) ran the `-scale` A/B first: HEAD's binary gave E5's line 0.875 / 0.871 / 0.883 ms, the final binary's E6 line 1.080 / 1.110 / 1.070 (median 1.080, over both 1.063 and 1.075), and its second run failed its own in-run check (`SCALE FAIL: ... 1.110 ms (<= E5's 0.881 + 0.2)`). That gate was stopped there (the battery it had started was killed and is not reported). Under the adaptive build the modified `RHSimMarket.cpp` and `RHSimLevers.cpp` are separate translation units (`[Adaptive Build] Excluded from RedHopeSim unity file: ...`), so `RollMarket`'s one walk of the rules called `TradeRuleRetiresAt`, defined in `RHSimLevers.cpp`, out of line for every rule at every roll; moved inline into the header, body unchanged, the E6 line fell to 0.958 / 0.962 / 1.027 with the same 13 digests, and the whole gate below was run again from that build, the mutations included. **D10's retirement itself had no check** (no `-levers` check read which rules retire, so a broken retirement test would have passed every suite but `-scale`'s rule count); LV3 (d) reads it roll by roll now, and mutations 33 and 34 turn it red.

### E8's frame bar: the director's answer (2026-10-29)

From the orchestrator's question L (`docs/qa/2026-10-25/e8-market-panel-design.md`, DIRECTOR ANSWER (2026-10-29)), on R2-7's bar (P1's median and p95 within 1.0 ms of P0's "in every pair", set on D8's +0.11 / -0.19 ms noise): **(a) judge on quiet pairs.** A pair counts only when `uptime`'s 1-minute load is under 5. Each scene and resolution takes three counted adjacent pairs, and the bar is the median of their three deltas: at most 1.0 ms for the median frame time and for p95. The `Market` slot stays a hard bar on every counted pair (0.2 ms a frame, 2 ms for the worst rebuild), so a real cost of 1 ms or more still fails. The reason is that on this 8 GB machine the noise is larger than the bar: the sites gate's quiet pairs reached +1.52 ms and its busy pairs swung from about -8 to +10 ms, and D6e's two DeepBench runs of one unchanged binary differed by 1.31 ms (median) and 1.26 ms (p95). It is the method the director accepted for the sites gate (2026-10-26). Not taken: (b) every pair strictly, which would likely stop E8 on noise; (c) the in-process slot budgets alone, which measure the panel's processing time, not the graphics card's work drawing the Routes overlay. The operational rules (when the load is read, the fallback if the editor alone holds it at 5 or more, the 45-minute bound) are ruling 18 in `docs/qa/2026-10-26/preflight/ORCHESTRATOR-RULINGS.md`; `e8-gate-wf.js` item 9 and its gate lens apply them.

### D6e lift and tram power: what it settles, and where it deviated (2026-10-28, not yet committed)

Built from `docs/qa/2026-10-26/preflight/D6e-brief.md` on E6's source (`7adc7ee`, save v57). The tree sits on `01f5299`, the docs-only T1 commit made while D6e was being built (`git diff 7adc7ee 01f5299 -- Source docs/data Content scripts` is empty), so D6e commits on `01f5299`. The order of authority, in the queue's order: the DIRECTOR ANSWERs (`docs/qa/2026-10-22/d6-caverns-design.md` Q-A (a), Q-B (a), **Q-C (a): trams carry people only** - no robot tram edge, hold, ride or reserve term; `docs/qa/2026-10-23/d8-deep-view-design.md` **Q-C (a) with R7**: the served-capacity bar ships inside D6e) > `ORCHESTRATOR-RULINGS.md` (1, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9) > `CROSS-CHECK.md` section 6 (items 1, 14, 15) > the brief > the REFRESH AT 31ffa6f > MERGED section 5. Superseded and not built: the draft's section 7 (40 W, 2 W, priority 8, `-liftpower`) and "Save v51" with `OutError` refusals.

**What D6e builds.** (The three rows are placeholders awaiting the director.)
- **Rows** (`docs/data/RH_Config.csv` after `TramPlacesPerSol`, `DT_Config` synced from the whole CSV with `rh_sync_datatables.py`, 316 -> 319 rows): `LiftCarW` 200 W a fitted car, `TramWPerCell` 5 W a chain point, `TransitLoadPriority` 6 (unclamped, like `CoolingLoadPriority`; the draws clamped at 0). Header defaults equal the CSV.
- **Load entries.** `StepPower`'s `FLoadEntry` gains `uint8 Kind` (0 building, 1 cooling, 2 lift, 3 tram) and `int32 Index`. Only with `bHasTransit` (the first car), after D5's cooling entries: one entry per fitted shaft in Id order (`Cars x LiftCarW`), then one per tram line in Id order (`GetTunnelChainLength(StopA, StopB) x TramWPerCell`), counted in `TransitEntries`. With no car nothing is appended and the step is D5's code.
- **RC 7.** Both gates read `(CoolingEntries + TransitEntries) > 0` (the scraping test and the walk). The walk's order is priority, then buildings, cooling, lifts, trams among equals, then the deeper floor among cooling, the lower shaft Id among lifts and the lower line Id among trams. It is built in two parts (see the deviation "the lift and tram entries are merged, not sorted"): the buildings and the cooling entries are sorted alone, by D5's comparator, as the same array D5 sorted; the lift and tram entries, sorted by Kind and Id, are then inserted after the last entry of equal or lower priority. With no transit entry it is D5's sort exactly. In the walk `ShedFloors` counts Kind 1 only, `ShortMask` reads Kind 1 only, and a lift or tram entry in the walked prefix calls `NoteTransitShortMs`. `StepDepthWarmth`'s third argument (`CoolingEntries > 0`), `CoolingW` and `CoolingFloors` are unchanged.
- **The rings (option (a)).** `FRHTransitLedger` and `FRHTramLine` gain runtime `ShortSol[2] = {-1,-1}` and `ShortMs[2] = {0,0}`; `WriteTransitBlock` and `WriteTramBlock` serialize named fields, so their bytes do not move (TR18's and TM6's layout lines are unchanged in the battery). `NoteTransitShortMs` (in `RHSimTransit.cpp`, reusing `TransitSolOf`) tags the slot `sol % 2` with the sol of `GetStepEndSeconds()`, resets an older slot, adds `RoundToInt64(SubDt x 1000)` clamped at 1,200,000, and drops a write into a slot holding a later sol with a Warning (as `ChargeTransit`).
- **RC 8.** `Served = 1000 - min(1000, ShortMs(s-1) / 1200)` permille, read in `RollTransit(SolNow)` for `SolNow - 1` (complete: `StepTransit` runs before `StepPower` in both spines). Only the two capacity arguments of the roll change: a fitted shaft's wait uses `Hoist + (Cars x LiftPlacesPerSol - Hoist) x Served / 1000` (int64), a line's `max(1, TramPlacesPerSol x Served / 1000)`. `GetShaftCapacityPlaces`, `ComputeTransitWaitSec`, TR4's numbers and the robots' reserve are unchanged. Public const accessors: `GetShaftServedPermille`, `GetShaftServedCapacityPlaces` (D8's bar), `GetTramServedPermille`, `GetTramServedCapacityPlaces`, `GetLiftCarW`, `GetTramWPerCell`, `GetTransitLoadPriority` (the getters read `TransitCheckedSol - 1`); harness `Debug_GetTransitShortMs` and `Debug_SetTransitPowerRows` (TP1 (d) only). There is no `Debug_SetTransitPowerScale` and no switch that turns transit power off: `-transit` holds by its bank pin.
- **Save v58, frame `'RHD6'`** (`RHSaveFrame::TransitPowerTag`), written straight after E6's `'RHL6'` and read with `RHSaveFrame::Read` straight after E6's reader (so it consumes the frame): `int32 Count`, then per fitted shaft by Id and per line by Id `Kind, Id, Tag0, Ms0, Tag1, Ms1` (24 bytes; ms clamped again at write). The default colony writes Count 0: a 4-byte payload, 24 bytes of frame. Every repair is a Warning (`LoadColony v58: ...`), never an Error or a refusal: a lost frame and a count outside `0..MaxShaftsCap + MaxTramLinesCap` or not fitting the payload leave every ring empty; an unknown shaft, an unfitted shaft, an unknown line, a repeated Id or a Kind other than 2/3 drops that entry; a slot tagged below -1, of the wrong parity, past `TransitCheckedSol + 1`, or holding ms outside 0..1,200,000 is emptied. A repair costs at most one sol's served share.
- **The literal-version tests** (`git grep -n -P 'Ver == 57\b|"/57"|\(expect 57\)' Source`): 35 literals in 12 files moved to 58 (16 `Ver == 57`, 16 `"/57"`, 3 `(expect 57)`: the brief's 14 `Ver ==` / `/57` sites plus E5's CU10 and E6's LV9 pairs and the commandlet's `/57` and `(expect 57)` texts). No suite asserted that its frame ends the file (E5's CU10, XE10, E6's LV9 and MX1 all check "follows"), so none needed amending.
- **The served-capacity bar (D8 R7, the only UI change).** `RHSectionVisualizerSubsystem.cpp`: the lift label and the bar's `Cap` read `GetShaftServedCapacityPlaces`, the label drops ` (nominal)` (`Shaft %d · %s / %s places · wait %d s · %s commuters a sol`), the legend's long text drops `(nominal)` (the brief's UNCERTAIN default: simplest is to drop it), and the R7 comment is updated. The bar's hash already mixed `Cap`. Gate-D rows M6 and M8 carry the new strings; M6's "`nominal` goes when D6e's served capacity is shown" is resolved.
- **`-transitpower`** (`RHSimTransitPowerSuite.cpp`, `RHRunTransitPowerSuite`, dispatched after `-levers`; `FParse::Param` matches whole switches, so `-transit` never fires for it): TP0 the rows; TP1 D5 DP5's numbers with no car, the draws (+200, +800, +70, +150 W), the shed order at priority 6 and forced to 7, a shed lift not a floor; TP2 a Lander-only sol from an empty bank in both bands (1,200,000 ms, Served 0, capacity 200, 400 places wait 120 s against 0 s nominal) and the same on D5 DP6's floor; TP3 a rule-(ii) step (nothing shed, LoadW 220, +60,000 / +100 ms); TP4 era parity (three cars, six arrays: Served 612 agent / 550 era every sol, worst 62 <= 100; the bank full by day in every sol; onsets 38.2 s apart); TP1 (f) four tied WaterPlants keep D5's order when a car at 0 W is fitted; TP5 mid-sol save twins in both bands, the layout ('RHD6' straight after 'RHL6''s footer, found by tag; Count 0 / 4 bytes by default), the previous version refused (`/58`), thirteen doctored copies each one Warning and no Error (the emptied slots of the tag -2 and wrong-parity cases read back raw from a re-save as tag -1, 0 ms; the repeated-Id case gives the repeat different ms, so the first entry is shown kept); TP6 pinned capacity 1,000 / 4,000 and TR4's 60 s; TP7 a dark tram waits 600 s, not 0. TP4 reads the sim's own `GetShaftServedPermille` right after each roll. 39 checks. `rh_battery.sh` gains it (60 suites, 61 runs; header and echo fixed).

**UNCERTAIN items of the brief, each with its stated default taken.**
- The frame's payload layout (brief 2.6): the brief's own layout, `Count` then 24-byte entries, lifts before trams.
- The legend wording (2.7): `(nominal)` dropped, nothing added.
- DC9's delta (cross-check item 14 settled it): +24, observed.
- The ring storage (2.2): option (a), checked first (the transit and tram blocks write named fields).
- The lifts=1 playtest at 200 W (section 3, a charge-0 or no-delivery failure): did not happen - no stop, 0 failures in both the early and the final run; its other numbers move (below).

**Deviations.**
- MERGED section 10's item 6: **lift power cuts capacity, not ride speed**, and a lift's or line's own shortfall has no rating, arrivals or stranding effect: a dark sol raises only the next sol's waits (and, through them, the commute, `CommuteWaitCm`). **The draw itself is an ordinary load on the shared bank**: 200 W a car empties a scraping bank sooner, like any machine, so other loads shed sooner or more often, and those include life support (the AirFilter, priority 8) and the floor ratings that hang on it. That is an indirect effect of any load and is not special to lifts; the lifts=1 playtest below shows it at the placeholder 200 W. The rows are the director's to settle.
- **The D6e block is a framed tail block that repairs** with Warnings (ruling 3, option (i)), never a mid-file block that refuses.
- **SP1 adopted:** a line's capacity is floored at 1 place, so a dark sol reads a crowd as `MaxWaitSec` (TP7), never 0 (`ComputeTransitWaitSec` returns 0 for a capacity of 0).
- **SP2 adopted:** a shed lift or line counts in `ShedCount` only, never in `ShedFloors`; the POWER tile (`RHCommandDeckPanels.cpp`, `ShedCount - ShedFloors`) therefore calls a shed lift a "machine" (placeholder copy, unchanged).
- **SP3 adopted:** ms clamped at 1,200,000 when added and again at write, so a legitimate file never meets the "ms above one sol" repair.
- **The lift and tram entries are merged, not sorted** (the brief has one sort of every entry with the Kind comparator; the first build did that). `TArray::Sort` is an unstable introsort and two buildings of equal priority compare equal, so the order it leaves them in depends on the whole array: sorting the longer array reordered tied buildings - which of two AirFilters sheds first - with or without any draw. The first build's `-scale` showed it (below: two floors lost their rating and 12 colonists were recalled, at 0 W as at 200 W). The buildings and cooling are now sorted alone as D5 sorted them, and the transit entries are inserted at their priority; TP1 (f) pins it, and mutation 7 (the first build's single sort) turns TP1 (f) red.
- **Repairs beyond the brief's list**, each a Warning and each exercised in TP5 (e): a slot tagged past `TransitCheckedSol + 1` is emptied (no spine can stamp one: `StepTransit` rolls before `StepPower`; without it a doctored future tag would log the late-write Warning at every step), and a count whose bytes do not exactly fill the payload (too few or too many) empties every ring. TP5 (e) runs the brief's eight doctored copies plus five (a future tag, a repeated Id, a bad Kind, a count of -1, a count of `MaxShaftsCap + MaxTramLinesCap + 1`).
- **The count bound uses the compile-time caps**, `RH::MaxShaftsCap + RH::MaxTramLinesCap` (16 + 32 = 48), not the brief's `MaxShafts + MaxTramLinesCap`: a colony whose `MaxShafts` row was lowered after it sank its shafts keeps its rings. The exact-size test still binds, and an entry naming a shaft the colony lacks is dropped with its Warning.
- **TP1 (c)'s fixture includes the Pylon** that shaft 1 is sunk beside (priority 1, 10 W), so its full load is 680 W, not the 670 W the brief's list implies; the order it checks is the brief's.
- **A lost 'RHD6' frame always warns** (no ruling-2 "only when it held something to lose" rule was needed: no existing log loses the frame; the battery shows no `LoadColony v58` line outside `transitpower.log`).
- **SP5, a follow-up, not built:** the shaft card (`RHCommandDeck.cpp`, "load N / 4000") and `RH.Transit` (`RHCheats.cpp`) still show the nominal capacity.
- The new wording is placeholder: rows M6 and M8, and the developer-facing block A1-A7 in `docs/qa/2026-10-15/gate-d-wording.md` (prefix A, the builder's choice: free at HEAD per CROSS-CHECK section 5, `git grep -n -P '^\| ?A[0-9]+ '` found no row, and no brief claims it; ruling 6 assigns D6e no prefix; the orchestrator confirmed A as ruling 17). ### D7 atriums: what it settles, and where it deviated (2026-10-29, not yet committed)

Built from `docs/qa/2026-10-26/preflight/D7-brief.md` on D6e's source (`f039c66`, save v58). D7 commits on `8f04945`: sixteen docs-only commits landed during the build (`4e9a360`, `62a6ce7`, `da73d84`, `11652fa`, `7cd8690`, `de8ab59`, `73d3252`, `aa89e2a`, `f5fd628`, `5af7861` (rulings 19-21), `5382218` (the director's answer on D7's `-scale` under load), `e758a3d` (its correction with the full evidence, and R (a)), `c818305` (ruling 22), `353baac` (ruling 23), `2b48a9a` (ruling 20 corrected), `8f04945` (the director's answer S2); none touches `Source`, `docs/data`, `Content`, `Config` or `scripts`; `aa89e2a`, `5382218` and `e758a3d` add lines to this file and this entry only adds lines after them), so D7 commits on `353baac` and every anchor below holds there. The order of authority: the DIRECTOR ANSWERs (`docs/qa/2026-10-23/d7-atriums-design.md` **Q-A (a)**: an atrium converts a finished cavern, two steps, D6a's carving untouched; **Q-B (a)**: no stairs, floors change by shaft only; the placeholders stand; and its 2026-10-29 answer on `-scale` under load, **(a)** the quiet-rerun rule for D7; `docs/qa/2026-10-23/d8-deep-view-design.md` **Q-C (a)**: the atrium visuals ship inside D7, with D8's "Required by D8 in D7's build" items 1-5) > `ORCHESTRATOR-RULINGS.md` (1 item 4, 3 option (i), 6 prefix L, 7, 8: v59; 19, 20 and 21 settle three of review round 2's open points; 22 carries D7's quiet rule into E7's and E8's gates, and 23 lets a docs-only fix round keep a full run's evidence by the fingerprint recorded below) > `CROSS-CHECK.md` section 6 (items 1, 4, 11, 13, 15) > the brief (P1-P14) > the design's REFRESH, REVISION R1-R12, PROFESSOR REVIEW and draft.

**What D7 settles.**
- **Open, never removed.** An atrium is a saved list of cavern Ids (`FRHAtrium`, ascending, one a cavern). On every floor of the box but the deepest the box cells are *open*: a derived flag (`FRHAtriumCells`, bit 0 open, bit 1 facing, an open count per floor; keyed `AtriumsVersion` and `FloorCellsVersion`, built only while an atrium exists, compared under `-RHVerifyCaches`). No cell is removed, moved or reordered (AT2). The switch is `Atriums.Num() > 0`; every new branch tests it (or a floor's open count) first and every new key field is 0 without one (AT0 checks all seven fields with an atrium open and after its close).
- **The verbs.** `OpenAtrium` / `CloseAtrium` (Value = cavern Id) execute in `StepUplink` (the same index in both spines). `CanOpenAtrium` runs the ten refusals in the REVISION's order (no cavern or cancelled; already an atrium; unfinished, "N cells left"; one floor; an upper-floor box cell in use - furniture, a room, a station module, any floor building's footprint (every footprint cell, R6), a station key (a seat or the seat order), a tunnel chain cell, an open growth target (its Index cell or any of its Points) - naming the floor and the first cell in ordinal order; beds by a what-if `CountFloorBeds` (P9); walking: no split, no lost landing, an all-void dig allowed; the air bill through `GrowthBillFits` (the open quota's share and the breathing reserve stand); the per-floor air ceiling, the fix in cells N = ceil(excess x 1000 / (AtriumLeakPermille - 1000)) (P10); overlap in 3D). Refusals 6, 8 and 9 count only the cells each floor would newly open (`CountAtriumNewOpen`; the card reads the same count through `GetAtriumNewOpenCells`), so a box that takes in an atrium's open cells is refused by refusal 10's reason, never by a count that takes them twice (counted only when the box meets an atrium's box; otherwise the box's cells, as before). Every reason the card can show (refusals 5-10) says what fixes it, and so does refusal 3, which only the console's `RH.OpenAtrium` can show (the card lists only finished caverns); refusals 1, 2 and 4 and the close's rejection state the fact, and the card cannot reach them (it lists only finished caverns of two or more floors, and holds a second press while an atrium order for that cavern is in flight). The order runs the preflight again at execute, so a refusal 5-10 that arises while it is in flight (a box cell zoned, residents moved in, the oxygen spent) reaches the deck's notice as `REJECTED Open atrium None: ` and the reason - the `None` every order with no target shows there, as before D7 (L2, L14). Close is always allowed; nothing is refunded.
- **Air.** `GetFloorO2RequiredKg` and a new `GetFloorO2LeakKgPerSol` evaluate the exact expressions they replace on a floor with no open cell (the premium is a branch, never `+ 0`); `StepHabitability`, `Debug_ForceRateFloor`, `IsFloorSealedButSmall` and `GetStandingO2LeakKgPerSol` read them. The premium is billed up front (`TakeGrowthResource(Oxygen, PremiumKg)`, the store falls by exactly `PremiumKg`) and each upper floor's pool gets its share at once (AT10: to the bit in both bands, through the harness open, on a drained pool too).
- **Beds, homes, digs, walks.** `CountFloorBeds` subtracts open cells at both exits only when there are some; `GetCellBeds` is 0 on an open cell. `DeriveDeepHomes` covers every atrium floor (slots skip open cells); a mapped atrium floor keeps its homes in `HomeCell` (they change), an unmapped one writes `AtriumHomeCell` / `AtriumCellBeds`, never `HomeCell`. Dig labels flood non-open cells only (an open cell has `DigOf` INDEX_NONE; every reader guards it: `Touching`, `ServingShaft`, `IsRouteReachable`, the landing, `Resolve`, the load repair, the infirmary patient test). `IsWalkOrdinal` is the one step predicate: `BuildLatticeField`'s inline path, `LatticeAStar` and the deep-net landing call it, and `BuildLatticeNeighbours` and D6c's `BuildWalkFloor` evaluate the same test from the floor's flag row fetched once (for their hot loops; a builder's deviation, below); `BuildWalkFloor` keeps open cells out of every compartment, door and landing (AT13 pins the landing), and `WalkCm` answers "no walk" for one (P14). `Resolve` maps a position on an open cell to the nearest non-open cell by a 4-step BFS through open cells, distance first and then the lowest ordinal (P2). On load, `RepairLoadedRobots` treats an open cell as no cell (the surface deploy ring, with its own Warning), and the tail read's fallback remaps a robot on an open cell by Resolve's rule (AT9 runs both). New key fields: `FRHDigInfo`, `FRHDeepNet`, `FRHReserveMemo` (P4), `FRHDeepHomes`, the membership key (while a deep district exists), the commute key (inside `AnyMapped()`), `FRHDeepWalk` (both copies of each key, P8). Footholds (R9): a cavern's (and so D6b growth's) and a tunnel's start need a carved NON-open neighbour.
- **Hope.** `Out.Atrium = HopeAtriumMax x FacingHeads / Pop`, the last addend after `Out.Shelter`; a head counts once by home or seat (`GetAtriumFacingHeads`, cached on eight versions, `EnsureBedAssignments()` first, `-RHVerifyCaches` compared; a harness counter of its cached reads, `Debug_GetAtriumFacingReuses`, lets AT11 show its window reads it).
- **Save v59, frame `'RHD7'`** (`RHSaveFrame::AtriumTag`), written after D6e's `'RHD6'`: `int32 Count`, then each CavernId (a default colony: 4-byte payload, 24-byte frame; AT0 measures it in a saved file). Read twice (cross-check item 4): early, after teardown and `InstallWarmth` and before `RepairLoadedRobots`, by a non-moving read (`Ar.Tell` / `Read` / `Ar.Seek`); and at the tail after D6e's reader by the normal forward read, which consumes the frame - and installs the list, remapping robots on open cells by Resolve's BFS, only if the early read failed. "Lost" warns only when both fail. Every structural failure drops with one Warning on either path (AT9 runs all nine on both); the occupancy repair runs after `RefreshJobs`. `AtriumsVersion` moves at load only when the list was or becomes non-empty.
- **The rows** (CSV and `DT_Config`, synced whole, 319 -> 322 rows): `HopeAtriumMax` 3.0, `AtriumFillPermille` 1500, `AtriumLeakPermille` 2000, each "Placeholder, director review". No Struct bill, no power draw.
- **Presentation (const reads only).** The card (P5: a finished cavern of two or more floors is listed in the floor view) shows "Open as atrium" / "Close the atrium" ("Atrium order in flight" while one of its orders is in the uplink, when a press is held with a confirm line); while the open is refused, its reason on a dim line under the button (UI polish S1) and in the tip ("Not yet: ..."); else the tip's preview (the premium, the extra leak, the homes and seats that would face THIS atrium, "No home or seat would face it yet." for none; one formatter, `RHOrder::AtriumPreviewText`, for the card and `RH.AtriumGhost`); the air headroom of every floor of the box (after the open for a cavern that is not yet an atrium, with the cells each floor would newly open, refusal 9's own count; the hall's figure too); and Cut here. The card's lines are polled twice a second, and the cavern list scrolls past 240 px. Hovering "Open as atrium" draws the ghost (the cells that would open red-orange, this box's facing ring soft gold), redrawn twice a second while it shows and let go when the list is rebuilt under it. The cavern visualizer draws the railing (warm off-white), one tall warm light per atrium at its top floor's ceiling (hidden in the section with the layer), and a soft gold glow on the cells of the viewed floor that hold a facing home or seat (its own mesh, keyed on the facing count's inputs and the floor). The colony visualizer hides the open cells' tiles (and their lamps) on the viewed floor and shows the box's floors below through D8's rule `ShowsLevel(L) || (!bSectionMode && InAtriumBelowView(L, P))` - tiles (with the room props, furniture, labels and lamps they own), buildings and, through the agent visualizer, robots; only the carve tiles are darkened a step a floor down (their own material's tint); props, furniture, labels and lamps keep their own look, as buildings and robots do. A tile is born under that rule, so a load (which respawns every tile after it applies the view) keeps the void, and the darkening goes back on after the room and depth passes re-tint. The section draws no plate, band, wall, block or pip on an open cell; a railing bar on each edge where an open cell meets a floor cell that is not open; a thin warm rim on each facing cell's plate (D8's "faint warm edge"); and the light column (R3's fallback outline, accepted by ruling 19); it counts its railing bars and rims (`section.cut.atrium` checks them against the sim, `RH.AtriumStatus` prints them); `Pick` and `LocatePlate` skip open cells; its key takes `AtriumsVersion` only while an atrium exists. The CREW panel's Hope prose says "Atriums: N, facing M of P people" beside the Shelter line, with "(+x.x Hope for light and space)" only while the term reads at least +0.1. Crew wander re-draws a pick on an open cell, and a walk whose line crosses an open box goes round it by the box's ring corners (full figures and crowd figures alike). `OpenAtrium` / `CloseAtrium` read "Open atrium" / "Close atrium" on screen, and the uplink list's row names the cavern ("Open atrium #1", as its card numbers it). `RH.OpenAtrium`, `RH.CloseAtrium`, `RH.AtriumGhost`, `RH.AtriumStatus`, `RH.AtriumDress` and `RH.ClearTips` (captures); `RH.DeepBench` opens its cavern as an atrium.

**Review round 1 (2026-10-29, after the first read-only reviews).** What the reviews found and what was done (this round's statements about HEAD, the darkening, the light column's reason, the sixth textless button and the R2 mutation were corrected in round 2, and the card's headroom and the loaded `-scale` record in round 3, below):
- **The robot layer below the view (brief 2.8, R11, D8 R7 item 5).** The agent visualizer draws a robot on a floor below the view when the colony visualizer's `InAtriumBelowView(L, P)` says so - the one rule the tiles and buildings use (`ShowsLevel(L) || (!bSectionMode && InAtriumBelowView(L, P))`, now public); never in the section, and never tested with no atrium.
- **"Facing homes and seats glow softly in the overlay."** A soft gold fill on each cell of the viewed floor that faces an atrium and holds a facing head's home or seat (`GetAtriumFacingCells`, the facing count's own rule), drawn by the cavern visualizer in its own mesh with its own key (`GetAtriumFacingKey`: the facing count's eight inputs, and the floor), so it never redraws per frame and never redraws the cavern layer.
- **After a load the void stayed covered.** Every carve tile is respawned by a load after the view was applied; a tile is now born under the atrium rule (`ShowsCell`), and the view is applied again after the room and depth passes have dressed new tiles. The darkening is restored only where it still holds the value it wrote, so a room or depth pass that re-tints a tile (or a new material) is the new base, never overwritten by a stale one; a building added on the hall under the view is born shown. The click test's `atrium.close` now starts from a save and a load of the atrium colony on its top floor and requires 0 open-cell tiles drawn and the hall's tiles shown (the step count stays 97); the capture `d7_06` is taken after `RH.Save` and `RH.Load` on the top floor.
- **The card's air headroom** is the after-open figure for a cavern that is not yet an atrium whether or not the open is refused just now (`GetFloorAirHeadroomCellsWith(L, BoxCells)` then; since round 3 with `GetAtriumNewOpenCells(Id, L)`, refusal 9's own count since round 2), for every floor of the box including the hall; the card no longer builds a preview to draw it.
- **"N homes and seats would face it" and the ghost's ring** count and draw THIS box's facing only: a head facing another atrium only is not counted, and an existing atrium's ring on a shared floor is not drawn as this one's.
- **Tests.** AT7 refuses an Oxygen stock between the bill and the bill plus the breathing reserve (4 residents: a 30 kg reserve) by refusal 8 and opens with it covered. AT4 runs DeepCells growth in a Homes shape and civic growth in a Civic shape, each over the box and the rock round it, against a twin with no atrium (which zones the box), and checks the footholds directly (`IsCavernPointEligible`, `CanDigTunnel`'s start). AT9 asserts the early path on the nine structural cases, checks that the tail read's fallback warns nothing, and saves two Haulers on open cells (the rim (4,1) and the interior (3,0)) and loads them on both paths (TR18 (iii)'s method): the normal load sends them to the surface deploy ring with the open-cell Warning; the tail-only load remaps them to Resolve's cell, distance first and then the lowest ordinal ((4,2), not the spiral's lower ordinals two steps away; (1,0), not the corridor's (5,0) or (3,2)). AT1's refusal 5 names a station module that `GetProvidedRoom` answers (an Infirmary Module: "holds a station module (Infirmary Module)"), and adds the Lab Module's footprint, an off-centre footprint (R6: centred in a floor cell, reaching a box cell), a seat-priority key and a civic Index target. AT4's home cells carve the box first, so the open ordinals come before the residents' slots (HomeCell moves for 5 of 5 on the shape floor and on the tram floor); AT8's commute homes 12 residents (4 land past the box). AT0 builds every keyed cache with the atrium open (each field reads `AtriumsVersion`) and again after the close (each reads 0; the reserve memo is the seventh field). AT7 checks the bill to the bit, a drained pool, the colony's standing leak, and opens the 8 x 8 x 3 (6,400 kg). AT8 checks the lone cell's own dig and that no landing is in it, and a landing chosen between two candidates by ordinal. AT10 drains a pool before the open in both bands and shows the premium leak inside `StepHabitability` in both (no circulation for a quarter sol: 52 kg a sol on each upper floor). AT11 checks the facing count's own key: a carve alone, and a seat moved onto a facing cell.
- **A latent counting bug in the suite.** The log runs on its own thread, so a counter detached straight after the steps it watched could miss their lines (the M6c run of the first mutation pass logged its RHVERIFY Error but counted 0). Every counter now flushes the threaded log before it is read (`GLog->FlushThreadedLogs()`, as the currency, levers, market and transit-power suites do).
- **The robot load repairs** have their own Warning on the normal path (`Load: robot %d on floor %d stands on a cell open to an atrium - moved to the surface deploy ring`), so the open-cell branch of `RepairLoadedRobots` is observable (R1's labels alone would also send such a robot to the ring, with D4's text); a robot on any other cell keeps D4's text, so no other log moves.
- **Refusal 7's walk memo** is compared under `-RHVerifyCaches` on a reuse (the walk test runs again; an RHVERIFY Error on a disagreement).
- **R12.** The brief's prescribed cache of each floor's bed count alone brought the 2,000 preflights from 306 ms to 225 ms, still over the 100 ms budget; gathering refusal 5's station modules once a floor and keeping refusal 7's answer per (floor table, atrium list, shafts) brought them to about 31 ms. The budget passes with the two optimizations beyond the brief; ruling 20 settled it: no director note. Only the bed-count and walk memos are caches compared under `-RHVerifyCaches`; the module gather holds nothing to compare (round 3, below; ruling 20 corrected in `2b48a9a`).
- **Wording.** Refusals 7, 9 and 10 and L13 gained a fix (refusal 9 names a smaller cavern or floor, since an atrium always opens its whole box); counts are pluralised ("1 cell left", "1 home or seat"); "a"/"an" follows the building's name; `OpenAtrium` / `CloseAtrium` read "Open atrium" / "Close atrium" on screen (`RHOrder::VerbText`, L21); a refused "Open as atrium" shows its reason on a dim line under the button (UI polish S1, L22). The Hope line is in the CREW panel's Hope prose, beside the Shelter line the brief anchored it to (L12 says so; the brief and the design call it the City panel).
- **Smaller fixes.** The card's lines are polled twice a second (the tooltip's preview, the facing heads' derivation, only while the tip shows); a ghost the card's hover put up is let go when the list is rebuilt under it (a button destroyed under the cursor sends no OnUnhovered), and the ghost redraws twice a second while it shows; crew wander re-draws a pick that lands on an open cell (uniform over the cells that are not, 8 draws, then the next cell); `section.cut.atrium` counts the top floor's plates with the atrium open and closed and requires the difference to equal the open cells in the slab counted from the sim; the dead `IsAtriumFloor` is gone; `RefreshCavernList`'s header comment describes the widened list. The `-scale` atrium block raises its harness air, bank and oxygen before its first step. Three readers held a `FRHDigInfo` reference across `EnsureDeepNet()`, whose rebuild can add to `DigCache` and move the entry (`RepairLoadedRobots`, `IsRouteReachable`, the infirmary patient test; they predate D7): each now reads the label before the call or fetches the entry again after it (no counter moves).

**Review round 2 (2026-10-29, evening, after the second read-only reviews).** What they found and what was done:
- **AT11's "0 rebuilds over 1,000 unchanged steps" could not fail.** Its four residents on the hall -3 had no water: the colony was evacuated ("THE COLONY IS QUIET") before the window, and `GetColonyHope` reads the facing count only while `Pop > 0`, so nothing in the window read the count, and the case's close and reopen never ran it under `-RHVerifyCaches`. Now the case stocks water and food (2,000 t each; the pools are colony-wide, as DP8 stocks them), asserts 4 residents and the facing heads at the open (2), the close (0) and the reopen (2) under verify, and 4 residents and 2 facing heads before and after the window; it reads `GetColonyHope().FacingHeads` on every step (2 on all 1,000 reads) and counts the facing count's cached reads (`Debug_GetAtriumFacingReuses`): the window read it 2,000 times and rebuilt it 0 times. Mutation MK (a per-step field in the facing key: the clock's sim seconds) fails the check (below).
- **AT10's 10-sol comparison compared two empty colonies** (Hope 50.000 / 50.000, with nobody left). Now water and food are stocked in both bands; after 10 sols each band keeps its 4 residents, 2 facing, `Atrium` 1.5000 in each (asserted equal); the fills agree within one era step's fill taken from the row (`O2FillRateKgPerHour` x 60 s / 50 = 24 kg; the hall's pool now under its residents' breath: 1,699.85 / 1,700.00 kg) and Hope, with the atrium term in it, within 5% (43.420 / 43.421). The to-the-bit check says it is the harness open (`ExecuteOpenAtrium`) in each band; the uplink order is checked to open in both bands, and its pools are not compared to the bit, because the step that executes it also runs the habitability step.
- **Capture 4 showed neither the railing nor a facing edge, and round 1's "too fine to see" was wrong.** At Cut here the plane is the box's middle row, so the three-row slab holds only box cells: no floor cell borders an open cell there, and no railing bar was drawn at all. The section now counts its railing bars and facing rims (per floor and in all; `RH.AtriumStatus` prints them in the section). `section.cut.atrium` gives its atrium floor cells round the box on both floors (the column's first spiral ring outside the box, and a corridor (0,2)..(3,2) along its north side; every cell keeps a floor neighbour on the way to the column, so the open never splits the dig) and requires the bars drawn on the top floor and the rims drawn on both floors to equal counts derived from the sim, each above 0: 2 bars and 10 rims at its axis 0. The captures take Cut here (`d7_07`: the void, the light column, the hall's rimmed plates) and the plane stepped onto the ring row x = 7 (`d7_08` framed, `d7_09` from closer: 14 railing bars on -8 and -9, 37 facing rims, rimmed plates beside plain ones past the box's end).
- **The facing edge** (D8 section 3, "a faint warm edge") was a full-plate warm slip that took every facing cell's room or district hue. It is now a thin warm frame on the plate's rim (four slips 70 cm wide, just above the plate); the plate inside keeps its hue.
- **Refusals 6, 8 and 9 counted twice** the cells of a box that takes in an atrium's open cells (D6a lets a box take in dug points), so such a box could be refused by beds, the bill or the ceiling instead of by refusal 10. They now count only the cells each floor would newly open. AT1 adds the case: atrium 1 open on -1..-3, a finished box (4,-1)..(6,1) on -2..-3 over its open column x = 4 of -2 (a corridor (1,2)..(5,2) gives it a foothold), 12 residents on -2 with 19 beds: refused with refusal 10's reason (the double count read 10 beds for 12 residents). Mutation MD (every box cell counted again) fails it.
- **Tests sharpened.** AT0 measures the default frame in a saved file (found by tag right after 'RHD6', a 4-byte payload, the count 0). **Deviations.**
1. An atrium is a separate saved list keyed by cavern Id, not a field in the cavern block.
2. "Facing" is a 4-adjacency test on the atrium's own floors, with no line of sight.
3. Each floor's pool pays for its slice of the void; the slice's premium is billed up front.
4. People and robots change floors only by shaft (Q-B (a)).
5. A hand-made file with an occupied open cell loads with that atrium closed (a Warning repair).
6. Q2a's atrium brush is delivered as convert-a-finished-cavern, two steps (Q-A (a)).
7. While atriums exist, dig labels exclude open cells, so a dig is a walkable component.
8. The save block is a frame that repairs (option (i), ruling 3), read early by a non-moving read and again at the tail position after D6e's reader (cross-check item 4); the tail read is the fallback and the one that consumes the frame.
- Builder's choices beyond the list:
  - the `-scale` atrium block measures at 4,838 colonists, not the brief's 5,000: its setup evacuates 309 people for short rations before the first open (every budget has wide margins, so no verdict depends on it);
  - the furniture refusal sits in the placement path after `IsFurnishKeyValid`, not inside it (the load uses `IsFurnishKeyValid` and would Error-drop a piece instead of letting the occupancy repair close the atrium);
  - the placement refusal is the first underground test in `CanPlaceBuildingSized` (so a locked building over the void says "open to the atrium", AT4); footprint corners are taken 1 cm inside the footprint, so a footprint ending on a cell's edge claims no neighbour;
  - refusal 5 tests furniture before the room (furniture always stands in a room, so the room's test would hide it); `DesignateRoom` refuses zoning an open cell but lets a clear through;
  - refusals 6, 8 and 9 count only the cells each floor would newly open (refusal 10's overlap would otherwise be reported as a beds, bill or ceiling refusal);
  - the three rows' members sit in D7's own block of `RHSimWorldSubsystem.h` and are read beside `HopeShelterMax`'s read (`RHSimWorldSubsystem.cpp`, the config block's Shelter line), not beside the O2 rows' members and reads as brief 2.1 places them; the values are the same (AT0 reads them against `DT_Config`);
  - the section's light column is R3's fallback emissive outline (two posts at the box's along-edges on its first drawn row and a beam at the top floor's ceiling), not D8's unlit additive box: the project holds no unlit additive material, and authoring one is a new content asset - **accepted by ruling 19**;
  - the section's facing edge is a thin warm rim on the plate (four slips 70 cm wide), the plate inside keeping its hue;
  - the floor view's darkening step is applied to the carve tiles only; room props, furniture, labels, lamps, buildings and robots shown through the void keep their own look;
  - the Hope line ("the City panel line" of the brief and design) is in the CREW panel's Hope prose, beside the Shelter line the brief anchored it to (L12 says so);
  - R12 went beyond the brief: its prescribed bed-count cache alone took the 2,000 preflights from 306 ms to 225 ms, still over the 100 ms budget; refusal 5's station modules gathered once a floor and refusal 7's answer kept per (floor table, atrium list, shafts) bring them to about 31 ms. The bed-count memo and the walk memo persist between preflights and are compared with a fresh derivation under `-RHVerifyCaches` on every reuse (AT11 shows one reuse of each, compared, and mutations MV1 and MV2 show the compares run); the module gather is rebuilt on every call (a per-call map, `FindModuleOnCell`'s first-match rule), so it holds nothing to go stale and has no compare - rounds 0-2 said "both compared", as ruling 20 did until `2b48a9a`; ruling 20: no director note;
  - `-scale` and `RH.DeepBench` raise `O2FillRateKgPerHour` by harness before opening their atriums (their floors hold about 1,100 and 290 cells, already past one floor's circulation ceiling of 240 cell-equivalents, so refusal 9 refuses every box there) and stock the premium's oxygen; `-scale`'s block does so (with the bank) before its first step;
  - the card's preview of the facing heads derives the flags and home cells with the atrium list swapped for a copy that holds the extra cavern (a const read: nothing live is changed, the cache is put back), and counts only the heads facing this box;
  - the card holds a second press while an atrium order for the cavern is in flight (L23, L24), as the demolish button does;
  - crew walks round an open box by its ring corners (a straight-line router like the cab's, not a lattice path);
  - AT9's eight size-changing copies have their frame's lengths rewritten by the suite (`ReplaceFramePayload`), and every copy, case e's in-place edit too, is then resealed by `RHSaveFrame::Reseal` (the brief's helper; round 2's reason for not using it on the eight was wrong);
  - AT6's stacked case cannot tell the Atrium addend's place from a place just before Shelter (every partial sum lies on its binade's grid, so the two orders round alike); it checks the Total chain to the bit with 10 of 40 and 1..9 seat-only heads, and the place is the code's;
  - AT11's "1,000 unchanged steps" are 1,000 agent sub-steps, chosen so births and arrivals cannot change the roster; AT10's exact-at-the-open check uses the harness open (`ExecuteOpenAtrium`) from the same state in each band, and the uplink order is exercised in both bands;
  - a robot mid-trip when an atrium opens keeps its planned path until its target changes (review round 2) - **deferred by ruling 21** to a follow-up (option (a));
  - `IsWalkOrdinal` is not called by `BuildLatticeNeighbours` or D6c's `BuildWalkFloor`, against brief decision 10 and R2 ("used by all three robot neighbour generators ... and BuildWalkFloor"): each fetches the floor's flag row once (`GetAtriumFlags`) and tests bit 0 per cell in its hot loop, the same test `IsWalkOrdinal` makes (`LatticeAStar`, `BuildLatticeField`'s inline path and the landings call it); mutation M4a covers the first site and MW the second;
  - the card's air headroom counts the cells each floor would newly open (`GetAtriumNewOpenCells`, refusal 9's own count), so it agrees with refusal 9 for a box over an atrium's open cells (round 3);
  - the uplink list names an atrium order's cavern ("Open atrium #1", L21), as it names a demolish order's building.

The three rows `HopeAtriumMax`, `AtriumFillPermille` and `AtriumLeakPermille` are placeholders for **director review** (their CSV Notes say so); the strings that quote their values (L2 rows 8-9, L8, L11, L12, L14's open line) are flagged the same.
