### Gate 1, nothing flashes, day or night: what it settles, and where it chose (2026-11-04 to 2026-11-06)

James's answers of 2026-11-04 ("all A, go on gate 1": D1-D8 and D21 all A, `living-colony-design.md` section 8) authorise gate 1 only. Built from `/Volumes/Unreal/red_hope/wip-backups/g1/g1-brief.md` at HEAD `1c3db5f` (save v60) under the orchestrator's rulings 7, 18, 22-27; the design's section 1.3 for the scope, 2.1 (GFC-1, UI-1, SCR-V1, UI-V1, GFC-V1, GFC-V2, SCR-7, UI-2) and 1.4 items 7-8 for the reasons. The complaint (James's hand-play of the Late checkpoint, `wip-backups/living-colony/handplay-2026-11-04.log`): "everything is flashing". While the bank scrapes empty the shed walk cuts and restores loads on alternate sim steps, and every reader of the per-step flag (`bPowered`, `ShedCount`, the live `GenW`/`LoadW`, `IsFloorCirculated`) followed it. Canon: "photosensitivity: nothing may flash" (`GetLastBlackoutNight`'s comment, `RHSimWorldSubsystem.h:2625-2629`). The machines do run on the steps they are served (GFC-V1), so a rationed machine must read steady and dim, never off. Anchors below are at the final source. **Round 1** (2026-11-05) answered the reviewers' blocking findings on round 0's gate of record (the fifth final pair): the era band's shares that swung once a real second at 60x, the numbers that still followed the per-step pair in the floor's wait after a drain or a load, the Crew panel's and the guide's food lines that followed the grow lights' per-step flip, and DS11's clause 6, which held only because of how long N2 is. What round 1 changed is marked **(r1)** below; its gate ran on the seventh final pair (the sixth was superseded mid-gate, below). **Round 2** (2026-11-05, evening) answered five blocking findings on round 1's gate: the fold header's `USING` outside rationing, the live generation less a held net, which climbed with the morning sun and snapped back every 3.2 s; a speed-up into 60x that read an unserved load Rationed again with no service (round 1 measured a service and the watch against the current band's hold); the Crew layout line's worst-value hold, which delayed a fixed clash for a whole hold outside rationing and for ever while paused; the 3.2 s floor, which round 1 made the only on-screen guard for two transitions and which no mutation tested; and the POWER tile's false red 'short' (`-0 W`) for one floor at every end of rationing, with `RATIONING - 0 W SHORT` when the mean crossed zero. What round 2 changed is marked **(r2)** below; its gate on the r2 final pair is carried over in part by round 3 (round 1's, below, is superseded). **Round 3** (2026-11-06; James's option A of about 00:20, "one short fix round: the seat numbers get held steady like every other power reading, on both station cards, plus a new test that clicks a short-powered Lab Module at night; only the checks this change can affect re-run, as long as the sim build comes out byte-identical (if it doesn't, everything re-runs); then one review round") answered the one finding review round 2 left open (its code lens, blocking): the selected card's `SEATS: n of m` numbers still followed the per-step station set under a held ONLINE, so a rationed Lab Module read `SEATS: 2 of 2` and `SEATS: 0 of 0` on alternate steps, and this entry's follow-up called the case latent when the reference playtest reaches it at sol 41.61. What round 3 changed is marked **(r3)** below; no sim file changed (the RedHopeSim dylib is round 2's, byte for byte). Its gate on the r3 final pair is the gate of record; it re-ran what this change can affect and carried the rest over from round 2 (the round 3 gate, below, says which and why).

- **What it settles.**
  - **The shed observer (sim, runtime only).** `StepPower` (`RHSimWorldSubsystem.cpp:8662`) gains one line in the shed walk (`bRealShed |= E.WantW > 0.0;`, `:8857`, after `++Power.ShedCount;`; the flag is declared at `:8799`) and, after the D5a blackout latch, the observer block (`:8893-9001`): for every building in that step's load list it records the step end it was last cut and last served and the hold each earns, `ShedHoldFor(dt) = max(ShedHoldWindowS 50, 4 x dt)` (50 sim-s in the agent band, 240 in the era band), when it was first watched (again after a step it missed), and its served share as a running mean; for the colony, the last step a load that draws was cut and its hold, and running means of the net watts (generation less the wanted load) and of the served share of the wanted load. **(r1)** Every mean's time constant is the step's hold, `ShedHoldFor(dt)`: one sol-hour (50 sim-s) in the agent band, as the brief has it, and four era steps (240 sim-s) in the era band, where a sol-hour mean is shorter than one 60 s step (`a = 0.70`) and followed each step's value. The served shares (each building's and the colony's) count **whole shed cycles**: a cycle runs from the step after a cut (for the colony, a real shed) to the next cut, and each closed cycle moves the mean by `1 - exp(-cycle length / hold)`; the first cycle after a building is first watched (for the colony, after the load) sets it outright, and a building back after a missed step keeps its share. A load cut on every other step therefore reads a steady half at any step length, where round 0's per-step mean of the alternation swung between about 23 % and 77 % once a real second at 60x (the reviewers' finding). The net-watts mean starts again at a rationing episode's first step (a real shed while the colony was not rationing), as at the load's first step: a mean carried over from a 60x afternoon read hundreds of watts to spare, and `USING -360 W`, on the first dry steps at 1x (the uncounted `g1_r1_dev_flash2`). Types, getters and members in `RHSimWorldSubsystem.h` (`:2631-2678`, after `GetLastBlackoutNight`; `Debug_SetShedObserver` `:3254`; `ShedSeen`, `ShedColony`, `bShedObserverOn` `:3914-3916`, after `LastBlackoutNight`). It is never saved (`SaveColony` and every save frame untouched; `RHSaveVersion` 60), is cleared in `LoadColony` beside `LastBlackoutNight = -1` (`:14825-14826`) and starts empty in a new world. Nothing in the sim reads it: `git grep -P` finds `GetShedHold`, `IsColonyRationing` and the held twins called only by each other and by `Source/RedHope` and DS11. **(r2)** A service's hold and the watch follow the cut's rule: each building now stores the hold it must be watched before it can read Unserved (`WatchHoldS`, set from its first-sight step's hold), and a service's hold or a watch not yet met that is still in force at the last step's end is raised to a longer step's hold; one already over is never raised. The colony's net-watts mean is replaced by the running mean of the shortfall (`ShortWMean`: `max(0, the wanted load - generation)`, the same time constant and the same restart at a rationing onset): the signed mean crossed 0 in a sunrise while the colony still rationed, so the screen read `0 W SHORT`; the shortfall's mean stays above 0 for the whole hold after the last real shed (that step was short).
  - **The classification** (`GetShedHold`, `:2978`): Powered unless the building was cut inside that cut's hold; then Rationed if it was also served inside the larger of that service's hold and the current band's, or if it has not been watched for a whole hold; else Unserved. Release to Powered comes only after a full hold with no cut, so it is not keyed to the night latch and covers the morning after a blackout and a daytime storm (UI-V1). `IsColonyRationing` (`:3006`): a load that draws (`WantW > 0`) was cut inside its hold; a cut 0 W Solar Array, Stockpile or dome does not count. **(r2)** The service and the watch are measured against their own stored holds (raised by the observer while in force), never the current band's: round 1 measured them against the larger of their own and the band's, so a speed-up into 60x over a load already Unserved reopened evidence that had run out (Rationed again for up to 120 sim-s with no service, then Unserved: dark, dim, dark; the reviewers' finding, reproducible with the Lander switched off at night). The case the band rule was for still holds: an agent-band service just before the first era-band cut is raised to 240 s, so that cut reads Rationed. A record not watched on the last step (switched off, a site) reads Rationed while its cut hold is in force, never Unserved (its first-sight answer), so switching a machine on inside its hold no longer shows a stale Unserved for one step, then Rationed.
  - **Four held twins** (presentation only, beside each original): `IsFloorCirculatedHeld` (`:3011`), `IsHabNetworkCirculatedHeld` (`:3690`), `IsFloorSealedButSmallHeld` (`:3795`), `GetProvidedRoomHeld` (`:6476`): each the original with "the hold is not Unserved" (and not switched off, not a site) in place of this step's `bPowered`. The rating rule keeps the live `IsFloorCirculated`.
  - **The shared display helper** `URHPowerLookSubsystem` (new, `Source/RedHope/Public/RHPowerLook.h`, `Private/RHPowerLook.cpp`; a tickable world subsystem, Game and PIE). One mapping (`WantLook`, `:76`): Site while under construction, Off while switched off, Powered for an exempt building, else the sim's hold. One latch (`Latch`, `RHPowerLook.h:131`): a shown state changes at most once per `FloorRealS` real seconds, except a change into or out of Off or out of Site (the player's own switch, a site finishing), which applies at once; the first sight of an element is not a change. Per frame (`Tick`, `:103`) it latches every building's look and moves its glow toward Powered 1, Rationed `RationedGlow` 0.45 or 0 by at most dt / `FadeS` (dt clamped to 0.1 s, so no frame moves a light more than a tenth of its range); latches each floor's held circulation and fades its room-light level toward full, 0.30 while rationing is shown (today's brownout level, kept) or dark; latches the colony's rationing; and moves the bank bar toward 0 while rationing is shown, else the bank's fraction: re-targeted at most once per `FloorRealS` and glided to linearly over `FloorRealS` of clamped frame time, so it starts or turns at most once per floor (a bank that steps once a real second at 60x reads as one glide). `LatchBool`/`LatchValue` give readers keyed latches with the same rule. It prunes states not seen for 60 frames once a second; its maps grow only when an Id or key first appears and per-level state is fixed arrays (64 floors), so it allocates nothing per frame; it draws no random number. **(r1)** `LatchValue` carries a 32-bit value (a line's kind and its number latched as one); `IsRationingNow()` (`:319`: the sim's own unlatched `IsColonyRationing()`, or the shown latch) picks numbers, never a kind: while it holds, `GetNetW()` (`:326`) is the observer's mean, so no number on screen is built from the per-step `GenW`/`LoadW` pair while the shed flag alternates, and the shown net is latched through the floor like every shown state (it takes its source's value at most once per `FloorRealS`; every reader in a frame reads the same value), also in the floor's wait after a drain and after loading a drained save (whose latch's first sight consumed the floor); the bank bar's target is 0 while it holds. Each floor's light kind (dark, rationed, full) is latched as ONE value from the held circulation and the sim's rationing (step 4, `:202-`), so a room light never fades twice inside the floor because its two inputs moved at different times. The garden (step 6, `:257-`): the grow lights take the bank's watt-hours all or nothing each step before the grid's walk, so while the bank scrapes they, and the producing count, flip every step; the helper shows them dark, with a dark step's producing count, while a dark step was seen inside the colony's hold (sim seconds), else the live count, the pair latched through the floor (`AreGrowLightsDarkShown`, `GetProducingCellsShown`). `LatchWorst` (`:383`) holds a count where higher is worse at the worst value seen inside the colony's hold, then latches it. **(r2)** The shown net is ONE latched take of its kind (the rationing shortfall while `IsRationingNow`, negated and rounded up to the next whole watt; else the live `GenW - LoadW`), its value and the generation of the same instant (`Tick` step 3b; `GetNetW`, `GetNetGenW`, `IsNetMeanShown`), at most once per `FloorRealS`: a change of kind brings its own value, and while the colony rations the take that falls due is a change of kind, so a live take is never one step of the alternation. `LatchWorst` holds the worst value only while the colony rations (`IsRationingNow`); otherwise it passes the value straight to the floor.

- **Where it chose** (the brief's 1.4, built as written unless listed under the deviations):
  - **The real-time floor is 3.2 s** (`FloorRealS`, placeholder; the design's 2 s, raised): a 2 s floor lets an element change at 0 s and 2 s, which the probe's 3 s rule fails. The fade is 1.0 s (`FadeS`, placeholder, "about 1 s"); a frame's dt is clamped to 0.1 s inside every fade.
  - **The hold an event earns is `max(50, 4 x dt)` of its own step** (50 sim-s, one sol-hour, placeholder, in the agent band; 240 sim-s in the era band, 4 real s at 60x): the design's 50 sim-s window is shorter than one 60 sim-s era step, so in the era band "cut and served inside the window" could never both hold. A service counts for the larger of its own hold and the current band's, so the first era-band cut after agent-band service reads Rationed, never Unserved. After a 60x night the morning release at 1x waits 240 sim-s (4 real minutes) after the last era-band cut: steady, recorded.
  - **"Unserved" needs a whole hold of evidence.** A building first watched (after a load, a new world, or back after a step it missed: switched off, finished, demolished and rebuilt) restarts its evidence, so a cut on its first step reads Rationed, never dark; a building never watched reads Powered. Building Ids are never reused (`AddBuilding`), so a stale entry is never read for another building.
  - **Counting real loads only.** The colony is rationing while a load that draws (`WantW > 0`: buildings, cooling floors, lifts, tram lines) was cut inside its hold; the 0 W entries the walk cuts first (Solar Arrays, Stockpiles, domes) do not count. The tile no longer reads the live `ShedCount`.
  - **Elements are latched, whatever the cause** (1.4 (7)). Every switched reader's shown state passes one latch: the building look; the POWER tile's one state (rationing, short, surplus: its value colour, its sub line's kind and colour, and its value's sign move together); the bar's red/teal; the card status line's kind (switched off, resting, or the look; switching off and on applies at once); the habitat, station, circulator and vault-hint lines; the spare-watts colour. The two exceptions apply at once: the player's own switch and a site finishing.
  - **The battery bar is switched** and **the cooling line and the power chart are unchanged** (1.4 (8)-(10), above).
  - **The Air Filter draws 10 W idle, not 200 W** (1.4 (11)): `StepPower` charges a building `PowerIdle_W` unless a grid batch runs and the Air Filter has no recipe, so with priority 8 it is cut only when priorities 0-7 do not bring the load under generation. The design's "200 W against the Lander's 50 W" premise for the vault hint is therefore not what happens. The switch is made anyway (the hint and the room lights read the held state). In both flash runs, on the Vault slot drained at its 9.76 dusk, the hint read "Floor -1 is filling with air: N kg of N kg oxygen. Keep the Electrolyzer powered." throughout (its only text, steady), and the floor was rated at about sol 10.11 in every counted flash run of both rounds (`=== PHASE 1 EXIT: THE VAULT — floor -1 rated for the first crew ===`, in the segment's 8x stretch), as in the bot's own run, not drained (**corrected in r1**: round 0's entry said the floor was not rated by sol 10.53, which the logs do not bear out).
  - **Three held sim getters beyond the design's list** (1.4 (5)): a wider grep (sim getters that read `bPowered` inside) found three more card lines and one more guide branch that followed the shed: the habitat card's "no air circulation" line, the station's ONLINE / IDLE line, the circulator's SEALED line and the vault hint's sealed-small branch. They read the held twins.
  - **The 60x refusal check counts alerts** (1.4 (16)): a refused 60x stored in `LastNonZeroSpeed` still ends at the agent speed (the sim holds `LastAgentSpeed`), so `speed.space` counts `OnAlert` lines that start `60x unavailable` and reads the controller's resume speed.
  - **(r2) The 3.2 s floor has a mutation** (the brief's section 5 had none, and its reason does not hold): the brief said the per-event hold alone keeps every building look at least 4 real s apart at 60x and 6.25 s at 8x, so the floor would act only on aggregates and speed switches. That is false for the rule the sim has (round 1, the deviations): a load leaving Powered at a cut and a load leaving Unserved at a service are not held in the sim (DS11's edges phase shows each one step apart), so the floor is what holds them on screen, and it does so in the scripted runs: in the uncounted `g1_r2_dev_flash1`, `look #11 Forge` went Rationed -> Unserved -> Rationed 3.21 s apart on floor -1 at 3x, and in `g1_r2_dev_flash2` `card #36 IceDrill` went RATIONED -> SHED -> RATIONED 3.20 s apart. `g1_r2_mut_floor` (the floor set to 0 in the one `Latch`, `RHPowerLook.h`) fails R1 (the gate, below); the uncounted dev run of the same mutation, `g1_r2_dev_mutfloor`, failed `flash.vault` (the tile bar colour red -> teal -> red 1.85 s apart) and `flash.late.floor` (22 violations, among them the Water Plant's look Rationed -> Powered -> Rationed 0.55 s apart and the Forge's and the Ice Drill's Rationed -> Unserved -> Rationed 0.52 s apart). Which steps fail depends on where the sim's edges fall against the frames, so the mutation's expectation is R1 on at least one slot step with `flash.setup` passing. The probe also gained an agent-speed sunrise on a drained bank (the vault segment at 8x through sol 10.25), where a marginal load can be released and cut one step later.
  - **(r1) The round 0 strobe measure, corrected** (the reviewers' minor): `g1_mut_hold` flips the look byte (`GetLook`), so it measured the building looks, the hum and the card's kind, not the lights: building glow and lamps read the helper's glow (faded from the latched look) and room lights its per-floor level, which stayed steady under it, and R2 never fired in round 0. Round 1's `g1_r1b_mut_glow` drives the light path itself (below).

- **Recorded facts:**
  - **The Air Filter draws 10 W idle, not 200 W** (1.4 (11), above), so it is cut only when priorities 0-7 do not bring the load under generation. What the Vault probe saw the hint do: in every counted flash run the Vault segment's hint read "Floor -1 is filling with air: N kg of 400 kg oxygen. Keep the Electrolyzer powered." from the drain until floor -1 was rated at about sol 10.11 (one kind, never the Air Filter branch; **corrected in r1** from "to the segment's end"), and the guide showed THE VAULT at the night's start; the `vault` captures show the same line in all four frames before and after.
  - **The playtest's shed share aliases** at `-fps=10` x 16x (1.4 (12)): it samples every 16 steps, so a two-step alternation can read 0 % (the storm sols 12-14 read `short 100% shed 0%`, `checkpoint_Late.txt:94-106`); the slots' sols rest on `bank-min`, not on the shed share.
  - **After a 60x night the morning release at 1x waits 240 sim-s** (4 real minutes) after the last era-band cut: an era-band cut holds 240 sim-s, and a hold already over is never re-held (DS11's era clause: hold 240 s, every load stamped at the last step).
  - **(r1) What the hold rule bounds, per transition** (DS11's edges phase X, sol 16's dusk, the Electrolyzer driven with the bank pinned): a stay in Rationed lasts at least a hold less one step (49 s in 1 s steps; 180 s in the era band); a release to Powered comes a full hold (the cut's) after the last cut; an Unserved comes a full hold after the last service and after a hold watched. A load leaves Powered at its first cut and leaves Unserved at its first service, so in the sim Powered -> Rationed can follow a release, and Unserved -> Rationed an Unserved, one step later: the phase reads `RURURPR` with the gaps 49, 1, 50, 1, 49 and 1 s. On screen the helper's 3.2 s floor holds every change. Round 0's clause 6 ("any two changes of one load at least a hold apart") held only because N2 is 150 steps long and starts from a Rationed load (the reviewers' finding); round 1 restates it per transition (the deviations).
  - **(r1) A speed-up mid-scrape** (DS11's phase Y): a cut's hold still in force when the step length grows is raised to the new band's, so no load is released for one era step only to be cut on the next, and the colony's rationing never lapses (the last 1 s step cut the Electrolyzer, the first 60 s step served it: 0 hold changes, rationing on every step). Without the raise (`g1_r1b_mut_raise`) the Electrolyzer reads Powered for one era step.

The `floor1` before frames happened to catch the room lights at full in all three (mean pixel value 30.5, 30.4, 30.2); the after frames read 18.5, 18.6, 18.5 (the rationed level, steady).

- **Deviations from the brief or the design** (each the builder's, disclosed):
  - **From the design:** the floor is 3.2 s, not 2 s (1.4 (1)); the per-event era hold (1.4 (2)); the classification and four held getters live in the sim (1.4 (3), (5)); the tile's sub line reads `rationing N%` and its value is the running mean; seven mutations in round 0 and eleven in round 1, not five; the sandbox presets; **(r1)** proof bar 1 restated per transition, the means over a hold of whole shed cycles, the Crew panel's and the guide's food lines held (each below).
  - **The latches stamp the frame's time.** The helper's `Tick` and `LatchValue` use `FApp::GetCurrentTime()` (real seconds at the frame's start) rather than `FPlatformTime::Seconds()` (the brief's 3.3), so every latch in a frame stamps the same time and a change is dated by the frame that shows it. The flash probe samples at the end of each frame (`FCoreDelegates::OnEndFrame`, after the helper's tick and the deck's paint) with the same clock, not on the core ticker at the frame's start. Why: in the first dev run the closest two changes of one element measured 3.19-3.22 s against R1's 3.0 s, because a change made mid-frame was seen at the next frame's start; one frame of more than 0.2 s at the wrong moment would have failed R1 with no flash. With one clock the probe measures the latch's own gap (every counted run: 3.20-3.22 s).
  - **One latched state per line, not per input.** The brief latches the POWER value's red/green alone (`LatchBool(Key('T', 0), ...)`); the build latches the tile's whole state (rationing, short, surplus) through one key (`LatchValue`, a byte form of `LatchBool` added to the helper), so the value's colour, its sign and the sub line's kind change together. While the live net has crossed zero but the state has not changed yet, the value reads 0 on the state's side (`-0 W` or `+0 W`), so its sign never flips faster than its colour; while rationing is shown the value is the running mean, never shown above `-0`. The card status line latches its kind (switched off, resting, or the look) as one key (switching off and on applies at once); the vault hint latches its branch as one key (the brief latched the sealed-small test and used the live short test); the bar's red/teal is one latched colour. Why: two latches over related inputs can each change inside the floor of the other (seen in the first flash dev run: the spare-watts colour, and the tile's green-red-amber at a drain).
  - **The bank bar glides between floor-spaced targets**, not the brief's 1 s ease: it is re-targeted at most once per `FloorRealS` and moves linearly to that target over `FloorRealS` of clamped frame time (`RHPowerLook.cpp`, step 5). The bank is the one shown quantity that follows a continuous sim value; at 60x it steps once a real second (one era step), and a 1 s ease settles between steps, so every step read as "starts moving after 0.25 s at rest", a change a second (R1). Found by the counted run `g1_flash4` on the second final pair (below): the first two pairs built the 1 s fade as an exponential ease (time constant `FadeS`), which keeps moving while the bank charges fast but settled between era steps when it charged slowly, about 0.4 % an era step. With the glide the bar either moves without a pause (glides chained back to back) or rests until the next re-target, so it starts or turns at most once per floor; it lags the bank by up to two floors (6.4 s), and no frame moves it by more than a thirtieth of the bar.
  - **A hold still in force when the step length changes is measured in the new band** (the observer block, `RHSimWorldSubsystem.cpp:8919-8925` for a building's cut, `:8968-8971` for the colony's rationing; the brief's 3.2 (b) records each cut's own hold only). Found by `g1_mut_exempt2` (below): at a speed-up from 8x to 60x on a drained night, the last agent-band cut held 50 sim-s and the first 60 sim-s era step could be one that served everything (it depends on the last agent step's parity), so the colony read "not rationing" for one era step and the bar followed the bank's alternation (R1 on the tile bar, 0.95 s and 0.09 s apart); the same lapse would release a rationed machine for one era step and take it back on the next. The service side already measured a service in the current band (`GetShedHold`); the cut side and the colony's rationing now do the same for a hold still in force (a hold already over is never re-held, so 1.4 (2)'s "a speed-up never re-holds a machine already released" stands). Round 0's DS11 did not exercise a speed-up while scraping (its era phase starts drained from an unrationed dusk), and its line was byte-identical before and after the fix; round 1's phase Y does (the recorded facts), and `g1_r1b_mut_raise`, which deletes a building's raise, fails it. **(r2)** A service's hold and the watch now follow the same rule (raised while in force, never once over), and `GetShedHold` compares only stored holds: round 1's "a service measured in the current band" reopened expired evidence at a speed-up over an unserved load (the classification, above). Built first, alone (`build_a0`), and dev-run with forced drops (`g2a_dev_drops1`: 120/0, five hooks, five retries) before any other item.
    - F1: `PushPress`'s up action checks `HoldsPress` (the located `SButton`'s own `HasMouseCapture()`, never `IsPressed()`; a `MouseDown` or `MouseUp` click method is never retried, nor (fix round 1) a `PreciseClick` one: UE 5.8's `SButton::OnMouseButtonDown` takes no capture for it ("do not capture the pointer for precise taps or clicks"), so the plan's capture test would have retried every such press and logged its Error; no project button sets a click method today, so every located button is `DownAndUp`; not a located button: nothing to check) and, when the press was lost, logs `RHClick: press dropped (the button lost its press before the release); pressing again, down and up in one frame`, sends a fresh down and the up in the same runner action, and logs an Error `RHClick: the second press was not taken either` if even that is not held. `SButton::GetClickMethodFromInputType` is protected in UE 5.8 (`SButton.h:284`, under `protected:` at `:267`), not public as the plan read it: it is read through a pointer to member formed in a local subclass that is never made (`FButtonClickMethod::Of`).

UE 5.8's `SButton::OnMouseButtonUp` (`SButton.cpp:423-440`) clicks a `DownAndUp` button only while it holds the capture AND `IsHovered()`; any pointer move Slate routes between the down and the up (a real mouse over the game window among them) sends a captor the pointer has left its `OnMouseLeave` (`FSlateApplication::RoutePointerMoveEvent`, `SlateApplication.cpp:5682-5830`), so the button keeps its capture and its press and loses its hover. F1's `HoldsPress` tests only the capture, so that press was neither noticed nor retried. Fix round 2, all in `RHClickTest.cpp`:
      - (a) Just before every release of a located button, `PushPress`'s up action re-places the pointer on the button's centre through the same synthetic move the press used (`SendMove(Pos, true)`: the virtual cursor and `ProcessMouseMoveEvent`), inside the one runner action, so Slate's hover is current when the up is processed (no OS event is pumped in between). A press with no located button (a world, text or viewport press; drags and keys) is unchanged.
      - (b) A press whose button holds its capture but is not hovered when the up action runs (`LostHover`: the buttons `HoldsPress` tests, a located `SButton` whose click method needs the capture) is a dropped press: the pointer is re-placed on the button while it still holds its capture, the held press is let go (`ReleaseAllPointerCapture`; the button keeps its hover) and the button is pressed again with a fresh down, all in the same action and in that order, with the line `RHClick: press lost its hover (the button kept its capture, the pointer had left it) on '<label>'; pressing again, down and up in one frame`, and an Error `RHClick: the press again did not get its hover back either` if it is still not hovered. It counts in `GPressRetries` (the unchanged `CLICKTEST RETRIES n` line) and in the new `GHoverRetries`; each scene logs `RHClick: retries by kind: capture n, hover n` just before its RETRIES line.
      - Why that order (each found in an uncounted dev run of this round, before the freeze). Pressing again on a button that still holds its capture makes Slate release that capture before it sets the new one (`FSlateUser::SetPointerCaptor`, `SlateUser.cpp:256-259`), and the button's `OnMouseCaptureLost` then `Release()`s it: it holds the capture but not the press, and the up clicks nothing (the first build, `g2a_r2_dev1`: the retry line, then up `handled=0 capture=1 hover=1` on the hooked `Buy +100`, `Close the atrium`, `Open as atrium` and `8x`). Letting the press go first and then moving the pointer back does not restore the hover either: `FSlateUser::ReleaseCapture` records the captor's path as the last path under the pointer (`SlateUser.cpp:299-303`), so the next move sends the button no `OnMouseEnter` (the second build, `g2a_r2_dev2`: `RHClick: the press again did not get its hover back either`, up `capture=1 hover=0`). A move while the button still holds the capture does restore it (the captor's path gets its enter events, `SlateApplication.cpp:5822-5836`; `g2a_r2_dev1`'s ups read `hover=1`), so the move comes first, then the release, then the down.
      - (c) The retry runs only before our release and only on a button that still holds its capture (a `DownAndUp` button clicks only on the release), so a press whose click landed is never pressed again; a lost capture is retried by F1 and never also by (b) (`else if`).

(hovered=0 capture=1)`; labels never pressed are listed at the verdict (`RHClick: test hook: n hover label(s) armed but never pressed: ...`). `harness.droppress` now presses `8x` with the hover hook, then `3x` with the capture hook (below; the main count stays 125).
